summary: Full Riftbound test pass: headless tracer invariants + monkey gameplay-flow + per-card playtest on N untested cards. Returns one merged report.

invariants.sample: [console] Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (Not Found)

findings.what: After clicking End Turn on turn 3, the game advanced to turn 5 (player-1's next turn) but player-1's already-exhausted cards were NOT readied during the Awaken Phase: Chaos Rune (player-1-rune-8), Fury Rune (player-1-rune-5), and Windsinger in base all remain exhausted:true. State shows dom.runeExhausted=2, dom.baseExhausted=1, resource bar 'Runes 2/4', exhaustRune moves offered only for the two newly-channeled runes, and the AFTER screenshot shows Windsinger still visually rotated.
findings.why_wrong: Rule 315.1.b / 415.3.a: during the Awaken Phase the Turn Player readies ALL Game Objects they control. Entering turn 5's Main Phase, every rune and unit player-1 controlled at start of turn must be ready. Carrying exhausted state across the turn boundary means the player cannot tap old runes for energy or act with Windsinger — a core turn-structure violation any player notices immediately.
findings.ruleOrCard: 315.1.b / 415.3.a (Awaken Phase — ready all controlled Game Objects)
findings.reason: Rules 315.1.b/415.3.a verified (Turn Player readies all controlled Game Objects in Awaken Phase). Trace step 22 confirms turn.number=5, activePlayer=player-1, phase=main, with player-1-rune-8-ogn-166-298 exhausted:true, player-1-rune-5-ogn-007-298 exhausted:true, Windsinger (player-1-main-11-sfd-138-221) in base exhausted:true, dom.runeExhausted=2, dom.baseExhausted=1, resourceBar 'Runes 2/4', and exhaustRune moves offered only for the two newly-channeled runes (rune-10, rune-4). Root cause: the Awaken phase onBegin at riftbound-flow.ts:195-223 (a) only collects cards from 'base' and 'battlefield-*' zones — runes in the 'runePool' zone are never iterated at all; and (b) for the cards it does collect, checks context.cards.getCardMeta(cardId)?.exhausted (top-level cardMetas field, operations-impl.ts:326) instead of the __flags.exhausted sub-field where every exhaust writer stores it via counters.setFlag (operations-impl.ts:526-533; writers at resources.ts:123, movement.ts:336/514, cards.ts:549, chain-moves.ts:461/976, effect-executor.ts:510/513). So meta?.exhausted is undefined and nothing is readied. The exhaustRune enumerator at resources.ts:111 gates on counters.getFlag('exhausted'), and its omission of rune-8/rune-5 in step 22's move list proves __flags.exhausted remains true across the turn boundary. The correct readyAll move (turn.ts:189-211) uses counters.getCardsWithFlag/setFlag but is never invoked by the flow.

findings.what: [invariant] no-console-errors: [console] Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (Not Found)
findings.reason: Reproduced: exactly one 404 console error at startup, seed-independent across R1/R2/R3. The monkey driver navigates to /login (monkey-drive.ts:48); login.html:109 unconditionally does `fetch('/api/auth/dev-credentials')`; server.ts:2432 returns `json({ error: "No dev credentials configured" }, 404)` because DEFAULT_USERNAME/DEFAULT_PASSWORD are not set in the playtest server env. Chromium surfaces the 4xx fetch as a console error, which monkey-drive.ts:44 captures and monkey-drive.ts:149 flags as `no-console-errors`. Verified live: launching the server without those env vars and replaying the driver's login flow yields exactly `[404] http://localhost:3000/api/auth/dev-credentials` and the identical console text. Subsequent /play loads never re-hit the endpoint (rb_token cookie survives the driver's localStorage.clear(), so auth.js:12 takes the /api/auth/me path and returns early), which is why steps 1–40 are clean. Fix options: return 200 `{available:false}` from server.ts:2432, or guard the fetch in login.html:109 / auth.js:19.

findings.what: Activated ability's 'next unit enters ready' replacement does not apply
findings.expected: After playing Sun Disc (satisfying Legion — one card played this turn), activating its [Exhaust] ability, and letting the chain resolve, the next friendly unit played should enter ready (exhausted:false).
findings.observed: Ability activated (Sun Disc became exhausted, chain item showed {duration:'next',replaces:'enters-ready',target:{controller:'friendly',type:'unit'}}), both players passed, chain resolved — but continuousEffects stayed empty and the next unit (Legion Rearguard) entered exhausted:true. No log line indicated the effect was registered or fizzled.
findings.reason: Sun Disc's activated ability resolves through effect-executor.ts:725-734 (case "replacement"), which appends the {replaces:"enters-ready", duration:"next", ...} record to draft.activeReplacements. That field is never read anywhere in the engine (grep: only the write site, the type decl at types/game-state.ts:509, and a unit test assert it exists). The playUnit reducer at cards.ts:546-549 decides entry state solely via hasStaticEffect(cardId, "enter-ready") — a lookup of the entering unit's own printed static ability — and never consults draft.activeReplacements or checkReplacement(). checkReplacement() itself (replacement-effects.ts:232-303) also scans only registry.getAbilities() for printed type:"replacement" abilities on board cards, which Sun Disc does not have (its printed ability is type:"activated"). So after the chain resolves, the installed one-shot replacement is stored but orphaned, and the next friendly unit falls through to counters.setFlag(cardId, "exhausted", true) at cards.ts:549. (Report's "continuousEffects" is a lorcana-engine term; the riftbound-engine equivalent is activeReplacements — populated but unconsumed.)

findings.what: Accelerate keyword is not offered as an optional additional cost
findings.expected: When playing Legion Rearguard with [1][fury] affordable (had 12 energy + 2 fury), the player should get a choice/prompt to pay the Accelerate cost so the unit enters ready (rule 717).
findings.observed: No pendingChoice, no playUnit move variant carrying an accelerate/paidAdditionalCost param. Unit entered base with exhausted:true, energy went 12→10, fury unchanged at 2. cards.ts hardcodes paidAdditionalCost:false with comment 'until optional-cost enumeration is wired'.
findings.reason: playUnit enumerator (lines 517-533) emits only {playerId, cardId, location} with no accelerate/paidAdditionalCost variant, and the reducer hardcodes paidAdditionalCost:false at line 560 (comment at line 556: "until optional-cost enumeration is wired"). Entry-ready check at line 548 is static-effect only, so Accelerate's optional cost is never offered and units always enter exhausted. Card ogn-010-298 (legion-rearguard.ts:13) has Accelerate in rulesText but no engine path exists to pay it.

findings.what: Second activated ability (Disempower + [1] + Exhaust → 3-Might Mech token) is missing from the parsed abilities
findings.expected: GET /api/cards/ven-087-166 should list two activated abilities; activateAbility abilityIndex:1 should appear once the card is empowered and ready.
findings.observed: abilities[] contains only one entry: {cost:{exhaust:true},effect:{target:'self',type:'empower'},type:'activated'}. The token-creating ability is absent, so it can never be activated.
findings.reason: Verified via getCardRegistry().get("ven-087-166") — abilities[] contains only [{cost:{exhaust:true},effect:{target:'self',type:'empower'},type:'activated'}], matching the reported observation exactly; the second activated ability (Disempower this, [1], [Exhaust]: Play a 3 Might Mech unit token) is absent. This is the same object served by GET /api/cards/:id (server.ts:1617-1619 returns registry.get(cardId)). Root cause: parseAbilities on the two-line rulesText returns only the [Empower] keyword ability from line 1; the second line's leading text-cost "Disempower this, :rb_energy_1:, :rb_exhaust::" fails the text-cost regex at parser/index.ts:3392, which only accepts "Disempower me" (not "Disempower this"), so no activated ability is emitted for it and the multi-split path yields nothing better than the single-ability result.

findings.what: No visual indicator that the gear is Empowered
findings.expected: After the Empower ability resolves (meta.empowered=true), the board card should show an empowered badge/class so the player can see it is Empowered.
findings.observed: Server meta shows empowered:true but the DOM element className is 'card type-gear exhausted card--exhausted' with no empowered class/attribute; screenshot shows no badge.
findings.reason: renderCardElement builds the card class list at lines 615–622, reading meta.exhausted (617–620), meta.stunned (621), meta.buffed (622), and meta.damage (673), but never reads meta.empowered. Engine sets meta.empowered=true (effect-executor.ts:712–719; typed at game-state.ts:92), yet grep for "empower" across apps/riftbound-app/public/ (JS and CSS) yields zero hits — no class, no badge, no styling. So a gear with meta.empowered=true renders with only 'card type-gear exhausted card--exhausted', matching the observed DOM.

findings.what: Cost-reduction amount parsed as emoji-code string, not a number
findings.expected: The static ability's reduction amount should be numeric 2 (from '[2] less').
findings.observed: GET /api/cards/ven-096-166 → abilities[0].effect.reduction = ":rb_energy_2:" (string). static-cost-reduction.ts does `typeof rawAmt === 'number' ? rawAmt : 0`, so this contributes 0.
findings.reason: Runtime check: getCardRegistry().get("ven-096-166").abilities[0].effect.reduction === ":rb_energy_2:" (string). Emitted by static-parser.ts:800 (`reduction: selfCostScopeMatch[1]` stores the raw regex capture, after index.ts:142 normalized `[2]`→`:rb_energy_2:`). Consumer at static-cost-reduction.ts:194-198 reads rawAmt from by/reduction/amount and does `typeof rawAmt === "number" ? rawAmt : 0`, so the string contributes 0 instead of 2.

findings.what: 'For each card with my name in your trash' self cost-reduction is never evaluated at play time
findings.expected: With N Shadowblade Lurkers in trash, energy cost at play should be max(0, 5 − 2·N).
findings.observed: canAffordCard/deductCost only apply meta.costModifier and interactive reductions; the static self ability with scope 'for each card with my name in your trash' is never read (static-cost-reduction.ts explicitly skips the played card itself and there is no scope handler). Card always deducts 5 energy regardless of trash contents.
findings.reason: deductCost (cards.ts:266-299) and canAffordCard (cards.ts:216-261) compute adjustedEnergy = max(0, baseCost.energy + meta.costModifier - interactiveReduction) + x + repeat (lines 235-236, 284-285). Neither reads the played card's own static abilities nor counts same-name cards in trash. computeStaticCostReduction in static-cost-reduction.ts is never imported/called anywhere in the engine, and even it (a) skips the played card itself at line 138-140 and (b) only scans board permanents, with no "for each card with my name in your trash" scope handler (grep found zero matches). The card definition ven-096-166 in ven.json has abilities:[null] (parser produced no structured ability), and effect-executor.ts:1162's cost-reduction case only mutates meta.costModifier when a triggered/activated effect runs — never for a static self-reduction from hand. Result: Shadowblade Lurker always deducts printed 5 energy regardless of how many copies are in trash.

findings.what: Optional additional cost '[calm]' is never offered when playing the unit
findings.expected: With calm:1 power in pool, playing Clockwork Keeper should prompt (pendingChoice or move variant) to optionally pay [calm] as an additional cost
findings.observed: playUnit executed with no prompt/pendingChoice; power.calm stayed at 1 (unspent); only a single playUnit move variant was enumerated. Engine's playUnit move has no handling for 'additional-cost-option' abilities (grep in game-definition/moves/ returns 0 hits)
findings.reason: playUnit enumerator emits a single variant per unit with no optional-cost parameter (cards.ts:517-533), and the reducer hardcodes paidAdditionalCost:false with an explicit comment that optional-cost enumeration is not yet wired into playUnit (cards.ts:556-560). No pendingChoice is created. Downstream condition handling exists (trigger-runner.ts:123, static-abilities.ts:227-228, effect-executor.ts:1196-1198) but the upstream prompt/variant is never offered, so Clockwork Keeper's optional [calm] cost cannot be paid.

findings.what: Conditional 'if you paid the additional cost, draw 1' trigger never fires
findings.expected: After paying the optional [calm] cost, an on-play triggered ability should go on the chain and resolve to draw 1
findings.observed: No chain item, no passChainPriority move, hand went 7→6 (only the played card removed, no draw). Since the additional cost can never be paid, the payoff is unreachable
findings.reason: playUnit has no optional-cost enumeration and hardcodes paidAdditionalCost:false on the play-self event (cards.ts:556-560, comment admits it). The card's parsed triggered ability carries condition {type:"paid-additional-cost"} (verified via enrichCards), and fireTriggers filters matches through evaluateTriggerCondition (trigger-runner.ts:275-277) which for that condition returns event.paidAdditionalCost===true (trigger-runner.ts:127). With the flag always false the trigger is dropped before addToChain, so no chain item is created and draw 1 never resolves — the payoff is unreachable.

findings.what: 'I can't be chosen by enemy spells and abilities' is not enforced
findings.expected: Engine target resolution should exclude Ruin Runner from enemy spell/ability target lists
findings.observed: Card grants itself keyword 'Untargetable' via a static ability, but the engine has zero references to 'Untargetable' — resolveTarget in game-definition/moves/cards.ts does not filter on it. Card def comment itself notes 'Engine support for this is partial'. Could not empirically drive an enemy targeting spell in goldfish mode (p2 never receives reaction priority), but code inspection confirms no gate exists
findings.reason: Card def grants virtual keyword "Untargetable" via static grant-keyword (ruin-runner.ts:13-21, comment at :10-11 admits "Engine support for this is partial"). grep for "Untargetable" across packages/riftbound-engine/src/ returns zero hits. resolveTarget (abilities/target-resolver.ts:64-161) filters by type/controller/location/descriptor-filter only — no clause consults grantedKeywords or a printed "Untargetable" keyword to exclude a candidate. The keyword handling at :252-256 is a positive-match descriptor filter (target must HAVE keyword X), not an exclusion gate. The spell-play target enumeration in game-definition/moves/cards.ts:891-901 iterates resolveTarget's result directly with no post-filter. So an enemy spell targeting "an enemy unit" will list Ruin Runner as a valid target.

findings.what: 'Your opponents' [Hidden] cards can't be revealed here' is not enforced
findings.expected: revealHidden move should be illegal for an opponent's hidden card at Noxus Saboteur's location
findings.observed: Card grants itself keyword 'PreventReveal', but the engine's revealHidden condition (game-definition/moves/cards.ts:1111-1130) only checks status/pendingChoice/hidden-flag/owner — no check for PreventReveal at the location. 'PreventReveal' has zero references in engine source. Card def comment says 'engine's reveal-action gate honors this once implemented'
findings.reason: revealHidden condition at riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/cards.ts:1112-1130 checks only state.status, state.pendingChoice, meta.hidden, and owner===playerId — no PreventReveal/location check. Card def noxus-saboteur.ts:16 grants keyword "PreventReveal" and comment at :10-11 admits "engine's reveal-action gate honors this once implemented". Grep confirms zero "PreventReveal" references anywhere in riftbound-engine/src/ (engine uses registry.hasKeyword for Deflect/Ambush/Hidden at cards.ts:76,425,1004 but never for PreventReveal). An opponent's hidden card at Noxus Saboteur's location passes the revealHidden condition.

findings.what: 'I can be played to a battlefield where there are enemy units' is not implemented — engine never honors the CanPlayToEnemyBattlefield keyword
findings.expected: With enemy units present on a battlefield and no friendly units there, playUnit should accept location=<that battlefield> and the moves enumerator should list it. Card def (packages/riftbound-cards/src/cards/unl/rengar-trophy-hunter.ts:27) grants keyword 'CanPlayToEnemyBattlefield' and its comment claims it is 'honored by the play-restriction check in move validation'.
findings.observed: grep for 'CanPlayToEnemyBattlefield' across packages/riftbound-engine returns zero hits. playUnit condition (game-definition/moves/cards.ts:398-449) only checks hasAmbush + friendly-units-at-bf via canPlayViaAmbush; there is no branch reading CanPlayToEnemyBattlefield. In-game: with p2-controlled cards on battlefield-player-2-bf-ogn-276-298, playUnit to that location returned CONDITION_FAILED and pw moves listed only location:'base'.
findings.reason: Card def grants keyword "CanPlayToEnemyBattlefield" (rengar-trophy-hunter.ts:27) and its comment (lines 12-14) claims it is "honored by the play-restriction check in move validation". But grep for "CanPlayToEnemyBattlefield" across packages/riftbound-engine/ returns zero hits. The playUnit condition's battlefield-target branch (cards.ts:427-449) only reads the Ambush keyword (line 425/430) and gates via canPlayViaAmbush (keyword-effects.ts:313: `return hasAmbush && hasFriendlyUnitsAtBattlefield && isReactionTiming`), which requires friendly units at the target battlefield with no alternative enemy-units check. With only enemy units present, hasFriendlyUnits=false → canPlayViaAmbush returns false → condition returns false at cards.ts:447-449. The keyword is never read anywhere in the engine, so the "play to a battlefield where there are enemy units" text is unimplemented.

findings.what: playUnit enumerator never surfaces battlefield locations for Ambush units
findings.expected: For a unit with Ambush (or CanPlayToEnemyBattlefield), pw moves should include playUnit entries with location=<battlefield-zone-id> when the corresponding condition is met, so the UI can offer them.
findings.observed: enumerator at game-definition/moves/cards.ts:479-535 unconditionally pushes only {location:'base'} for every affordable unit in hand; no battlefield locations are ever enumerated. UI 'Play Unit' options showed only base.
findings.reason: playUnit.condition (lines 418-449) accepts battlefield locations for Ambush units via canPlayViaAmbush, but playUnit.enumerator (lines 481-534) never emits them: the results loop at 518-532 unconditionally pushes only {location: "base"} for every affordable unit in hand, with no Ambush/CanPlayToEnemyBattlefield branch and no battlefield-zone iteration. Additionally the enumerator early-returns [] when not activePlayer/main-phase/neutral-open (488-497), so Ambush reaction-timing plays are never enumerated either. unl-120-219 (Rengar, Trophy Hunter) carries both Ambush and CanPlayToEnemyBattlefield (rengar-trophy-hunter.ts:16-33), so its battlefield play options are legal per condition but never surfaced to the UI via pw moves.

findings.what: On-play trigger does not create a Tentacle token
findings.expected: Playing Illaoi should put a 1-Might Tentacle unit token into play (rulesText: 'When you play me... play a [1] [Might] Tentacle unit token')
findings.observed: After playUnit resolved, base contained only Illaoi; no chain item, no pendingChoice, no token in any zone. Sandbox token panel lists Recruit/Mech/Sand Soldier/Sprite/Bird/Gold but no Tentacle — token definition appears missing.
findings.reason: Runtime check: getCardRegistry().get("ven-182-166").abilities === [{type:"static", effect:{type:"modify-might", amount:1, per:"token unit you control", target:"self"}}] — no triggered ability. Cause: adaptJsonCard (all-cards.ts:805) filters the JSON's [null] to undefined, so enrichCard re-parses rulesText, but parser/index.ts TRIGGER_PATTERNS has no entry for "When you play me or when I score," (only play-self at :3669 and play-or-hold at :3883), so the token-creating trigger line is dropped and only the static +Might line survives. trigger-runner.ts:80 filters to type==="triggered", so playUnit finds nothing to put on the chain → no Tentacle token. Separately, Tentacle is absent from RIFTBOUND_TOKEN_DEFS (token.ts:44) and TokenName (types/moves.ts:562), matching the sandbox panel observation.

findings.what: +1 Might per token static not applied
findings.expected: With 2 friendly tokens in play, Illaoi's Might should read 6 (base 4 + 2)
findings.observed: After adding a Recruit and a Mech token via sandbox panel, Illaoi's might stayed at 4. (Caveat: sandbox tokens are created with cardType='unknown' instead of 'unit', so the static may be filtering them out — but the on-play token would have hit the same problem.)
findings.reason: The parser emits `{type:"static", effect:{type:"modify-might", amount:1, per:"token unit you control", target:"self"}}` for ven-182-166's second sentence (verified by running parseAbilities on the rulesText; static-parser.ts:587-607). The engine's static-effect applier ignores the `per` field entirely: applyStaticEffect reads only `effect.amount` as a fixed number and adds it once (static-abilities.ts:343-356, specifically line 344 `const amount = (effect.amount as number) ?? 0;` and line 353 `staticMightBonus: current + amount`). A grep of the engine's abilities/ and operations/ dirs finds zero readers of `effect.per`. So with 2 friendly tokens Illaoi gets a flat +1 (→5), never +2 (→6) — the per-token scaling is unimplemented at the engine layer. (The reporter's observed "4" is likely a sandbox recalc artifact; the confirmed engine defect is that `per` is dropped, so the expected 6 is unreachable regardless.)

findings.what: Deathknell does not create Mech tokens
findings.expected: When Ferrous Forerunner dies, two 3-Might Mech unit tokens should be played to your base
findings.observed: Killed it via Cull the Weak (ogn-209-298); after chain resolved, Forerunner was in trash and base was empty — no tokens, no chain item for the Deathknell, no pendingChoice. Mech token type does exist in the sandbox panel, so this is the trigger not firing rather than a missing token def.
findings.reason: Repro (bun script, output above): sfd-021-221 parses correctly to a `{trigger:{event:"die",on:"self"}, effect:{type:"create-token",amount:2,token:{name:"Mech",might:3}}}` triggered ability, but when killed via Cull the Weak the Deathknell never reaches the chain. Two engine-layer causes stack: (1) the `case "kill"` in effect-executor.ts:429-438 only does `zones.moveCard({targetZoneId:"trash"})` — it never emits a `die` event and `performCleanup` (state-based-checks.ts:92-173) only reaps damage≥might units still on the board, so a spell-killed unit is invisible to `runStateMaintenance`/`dispatchUnitDied`; (2) even on the damage-death path where `die` *is* dispatched, `getBoardCards` (trigger-runner.ts:136-200) scans only base/legendZone/battlefield*/battlefieldRow — the dying card is already in trash, so its own self-`die` listener is never polled (listener-registry.ts:14 documents "plus a just-died card in trash for its own die self-trigger" but the implementation at :89 just calls `getBoardCards`). Verified: `fireTriggers({type:"die",cardId,owner})` with the card in trash → 0 fired / no chain item; same call with the card still in base → fires and pushes to chain. Not card-specific to sfd-021-221 — this is an engine defect affecting all Deathknell units killed by a `kill` effect (and self-Deathknell generally).

findings.what: Conquer trigger cost-reduction does not scale with recycled unit's Might
findings.expected: Per rulesText: 'Reduce its Energy cost by the Might of the unit you recycled' — the Mech played from trash should have its energy cost reduced by exactly the recycled unit's Might (variable amount).
findings.observed: Card definition (rumble-hotheaded.ts) uses effect.ignoreCost:'energy', which plays the Mech for zero energy regardless of the recycled unit's Might. Source has a FIXME acknowledging the placeholder. Could not exercise in-play because no moveUnit action was enumerated to get Rumble to a battlefield and conquer.
findings.reason: rulesText (line 76) requires reducing the played Mech's energy cost by the recycled unit's Might (variable amount), but the conquer-trigger effect at line 54 uses `ignoreCost: "energy"`, which waives the energy cost entirely regardless of the recycled unit's Might. The PlayEffect type (riftbound-types effect-types.ts:66-67) only supports a boolean/"energy"/"power" ignoreCost or a fixed `reduceCost: Cost` — no variable-amount reduction exists. The FIXME at lines 18-20 explicitly acknowledges this placeholder and that the engine lacks variable-amount cost reduction.

findings.what: 'When you draw your second card each turn' trigger never fires
findings.expected: After the second card draw in a turn, a prompt should appear to choose a friendly unit and that unit should get +2 Might for the turn.
findings.observed: Drew 2 cards on turn 1 via Meditation while Frigid Jewel and a friendly unit (Legion Rearguard) were on board. No pendingChoice, no chain item, no log entry, and Legion Rearguard's Might stayed at 2. Card definition (frigid-jewel.ts) has no `abilities` field at all — the trigger is entirely unimplemented.
findings.reason: frigid-jewel.ts:4-14 defines only rulesText with no `abilities` array. The engine's registry.getAbilities (card-lookup.ts:165) returns `def.abilities ?? []` — it does not auto-parse rulesText — so toTriggerableAbilities (trigger-runner.ts:71-96) yields [] and findMatchingTriggers never matches. Additionally, even if an ability were added, restrictionSatisfied for `nth-time-each-turn` only implements the `play-card` counter and explicitly returns false for `draw` (trigger-matcher.ts:105-117, TODO at 114-116). The "second card drawn" trigger therefore cannot fire.

findings.what: 'When I conquer, you may kill a gear. If you do, buff me' trigger is unimplemented
findings.expected: On conquer, an optional prompt to kill a gear; if accepted, Adaptatron gets a +1 Might buff.
findings.observed: Card definition (adaptatron.ts) has no `abilities` field — the conquer trigger is entirely absent, so it can never fire. Could not exercise conquer in-play (no moveUnit enumerated), but the definition guarantees the rulesText behavior is missing.
findings.reason: adaptatron.ts:4-16 defines the UnitCard with rulesText "When I conquer, you may kill a gear. If you do, buff me" but no `abilities` field. The engine wires triggered abilities via the card's `abilities: Ability[]` array (see viktor-innovator.ts for the pattern; trigger-matcher.ts consumes it). No alternate registry references ogn-056-298 or adaptatron beyond the index export and all-cards list. The conquer→kill-gear→buff trigger is therefore unimplemented.

findings.what: [Weaponmaster] on-play does not fire
findings.expected: When Jax is played, an optional prompt to Equip one of your Equipment to him for [rainbow] less (Hand Hammer was in hand, so a valid target existed).
findings.observed: Playing Jax produced no pendingChoice, no chain item, no prompt. Card definition (jax-unrelenting.ts) has no `abilities` and no `keywords` — Weaponmaster is not declared.
findings.reason: jax-unrelenting.ts:4-18 defines the UnitCard with only cardNumber/cardType/domain/energyCost/id/isChampion/might/name/rarity/rulesText/setId/tags — no `abilities` array and no `keywords` array. The engine's registry reads abilities verbatim from the def (card-lookup.ts:164-166 `getAbilities` returns `definitions.get(cardId)?.abilities ?? []`) and keyword lookup checks only `def.keywords` or `abilities[].type==="keyword"` (card-lookup.ts:120-131). With both absent, play-time trigger evaluation (cards.ts:28-29, :552 fireTriggers on play-self) finds nothing for Jax, so no pendingChoice/chain/prompt is created. The [Weaponmaster] token exists only in rulesText (line 15), which the runtime does not parse. Claim that Weaponmaster is undeclared on sfd-119-221 is verified at file:line.

findings.what: 'When you attach an Equipment to me, you may pay [1] to draw 1' trigger is unimplemented
findings.expected: Attaching an Equipment to Jax should offer an optional pay-1-draw-1.
findings.observed: No such ability exists on the card definition; playing Hand Hammer alongside Jax produced no attach interaction and no draw prompt (hand size unchanged, energy unchanged apart from gear cost).
findings.reason: jax-unrelenting.ts:4-18 defines the UnitCard with only static data (cost, might, rulesText, tags) and no `abilities` field. The rulesText at line 15 declares "When you attach an Equipment to me, you may pay [1] to draw 1", but no triggered ability implements it. Compare card-sharp.ts:15-28 where an `abilities: Ability[]` array with `{type: "triggered", trigger: {...}, effect: {...}}` is present and attached to the card object. Grep across riftbound-engine and riftbound-cards for `sfd-119-221`/`jaxUnrelenting` shows only the card def, the sfd/index.ts re-export, and data/all-cards.ts registration — no separate ability registration exists. The Weaponmaster keyword itself is engine-handled (keyword-effects.ts:172), but the second-line pay-1-draw-1 attach trigger has no implementation anywhere.

findings.what: Self-buff on play has no effect on might or buffed state
findings.expected: After 'When you play me, buff me' resolves, Peak Guardian should have buffed=true and effective might 6 (base 5 + 1 buff)
findings.observed: meta.buffed stays false, might stays 5. Only meta.__flags.buffed becomes true. Root cause: effect-executor.ts:452 writes buff via counters.setFlag() → cardMetas[id].__flags.buffed, but getEffectiveMight (effect-executor.ts:149), while-buffed (static-abilities.ts:132), target-resolver.ts:227 all read meta?.buffed (top-level), which is never written.
findings.reason: Write path: effect-executor.ts:452 calls ctx.counters.setFlag(targetId, "buffed", true), whose core impl (packages/core/src/operations/operations-impl.ts:526-533) stores to state.cardMetas[id].__flags.buffed. Read paths: getEffectiveMight at effect-executor.ts:149 reads meta?.buffed; static-abilities.ts:132 reads meta?.buffed; target-resolver.ts:227 reads meta?.buffed. getCardMeta (operations-impl.ts:324-327) returns the raw cardMetas[id] object without lifting __flags, so meta.buffed is always undefined after a buff. Peak Guardian (ogn-223-298, might 5, "When you play me, buff me") therefore stays at effective might 5 with buffed=false. Root cause: effect-executor.ts case 'replacement' (line 725) stores the effect into draft.activeReplacements, but checkReplacement() (replacement-effects.ts:232) only scans board-card ability definitions and never reads draft.activeReplacements — spell-installed replacements are dead state.
findings.reason: Imperial Decree parses to a spell effect {type:"replacement", replaces:"take-damage", duration:"turn"} (parser/index.ts:4859-4864; wave4-cards.test.ts:258-263). effect-executor.ts case 'replacement' (:725-734) pushes it into draft.activeReplacements with a "consumer wiring is TODO" comment. checkReplacement() (replacement-effects.ts:232-303) iterates only base+battlefield cards via zones.getCardsInZone and reads registry.getAbilities(card.id) — grep shows zero references to activeReplacements in that file, and game-state.ts:505-509 documents activeReplacements as something checkReplacement "may" consult in future. The take-damage path (effect-executor.ts:393-396) calls checkReplacement, gets null (spell isn't on board), and applies normal damage — so Peak Guardian (5 might) takes 3 and survives.

findings.expected: Per the ruling: playing Thrill of the Hunt banishes a friendly unit, then adds it to the chain as a pending item [354.2/354.3]. When the spell finishes resolving, Abandoned Hall's 'when a player plays a spell' trigger becomes pending AFTER the unit [419.4.a/383.2.c]. Pending items finalize in append order [337.1.b], so the unit resolves onto Abandoned Hall first, then the trigger's target is chosen — the replayed unit IS a valid choice for the +1 Might buff.
findings.observed: Set up goldfish game with Abandoned Hall (unl-205-219) as player-1's battlefield via a custom saved deck. Played Trusty Ramhound (sfd-159-221) to base, then cast Thrill of the Hunt (unl-184-219) and passed priority. Result: Ramhound moved to the 'banishment' zone and stayed there — it was NEVER replayed to any location. The replayed unit is NOT offered as a target because it never arrives on board.
findings.notes: Root cause is upstream of the ordering question the ruling addresses: the engine's replay-via-spell mechanic is stubbed. In /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effect-executor.ts: (1) case 'sequence' (L929-935) loops sub-effects without wiring pendingValue:{source:0}, so target:{type:'pending-value'} resolves to []; (2) case 'play' (L1057-1069) is a stub — hardcodes targetZoneId:'base', ignores toLocation:{battlefield:'any'}, and does NOT add the card to the chain as a pending item per rule 354.2. Consequently the unit stays banished and the ordering described in the ruling (unit finalized before trigger target chosen) cannot occur. Arcane Shift (sfd-200-221) has no abilities/effect definition at all, so Thrill of the Hunt was used as the ruling explicitly names it as an equivalent example. findings.expected: Per the ruling: at finalization (when Alpha Strike goes on the chain) the caster (a) chooses a friendly unit as an explicit target, then (b) chooses UP TO N enemy units at battlefields where N = that friendly unit's current might, and may choose fewer (including zero). All chosen units are locked in as targets on the chain item.
findings.observed: Board: friendly Mech (might 3) at BF1, 5 enemy Recruits + 1 enemy Mech at BF2, Alpha Strike in hand, 7 energy. Engine offers NO playSpell move for Alpha Strike; direct POST /move playSpell returns CONDITION_FAILED. Code inspection confirms: (1) the friendly unit is not a chain target — it is an amount expression `{might:{controller:"friendly",type:"unit"}}` which resolveAmount() (effect-executor.ts:183-223) does not handle (only `might:"self"` is implemented → returns 0); (2) enemy units are `quantity:"all"` with `split:true`, but the playSpell enumerator/reducer stores NO targets for sequence effects (cards.ts:902-907, 957) and `split` has zero handling anywhere in the engine — no up-to-N caster choice exists; (3) spellEffectHasLegalTargets (cards.ts:335-336) recurses into the for-each `filter:"damaged"` sub-target and requires it non-empty at play time, so Alpha Strike is unplayable unless a damaged enemy already exists.
findings.notes: Rule 355.14 split-target selection is entirely unimplemented in the engine. The card definition at packages/riftbound-cards/src/cards/unl/alpha-strike.ts models neither the friendly-unit choice nor the enemy split-target choice as finalization-time targets. Secondary bugs surfaced during setup: addToken registers the token def under definitionId rather than the instance id, so registry.get(instanceId) returns undefined and tokens fail type=unit target filters; and the playSpell condition ctx (cards.ts:793-804) omits getCardMeta, so filter:"damaged" can never match there. findings.expected: Alpha Strike is playable when a friendly unit exists and there are enemy units at battlefields. At finalization the caster chooses the friendly unit and the enemy-unit targets; at RESOLUTION the caster distributes damage equal to the friendly unit's current Might across those targets, with each target receiving ≥1 and all damage distributed (rules 355.14.e-g, 359.3.f.2).
findings.observed: With a valid board (friendly Playful Phantom might=5 at base; 3 enemy units at a battlefield; 20 energy + calm/body power), the engine never offers playSpell for Alpha Strike and executeMove('playSpell',{cardId:'player-1-main-999-unl-192-219'}) returns CONDITION_FAILED. Code inspection confirms the split-damage ruling is unreachable and unimplemented: (1) spellEffectHasLegalTargets rejects the play because the second sequence sub-effect (for-each, target filter:'damaged', no quantity) is treated as a required caster-chosen target, and the play-condition ctx lacks getCardMeta so 'damaged' always evaluates false; (2) the damage-effect executor (effect-executor.ts case 'damage') ignores split:true and applies the full amount to EVERY target — there is no distribution prompt at resolution and no ≥1-per-target enforcement; (3) resolveAmount only handles might:'self', so amount:{might:{controller:'friendly',type:'unit'}} resolves to 0 — there is no 'choose a friendly unit' step at all; (4) targets are quantity:'all' (auto-selected), not caster-chosen at finalization as the ruling assumes.
findings.notes: Screenshot: /tmp/ruling-da6fb2fa426580ff.png. Setup: goldfish game 0bb2499f-d60f-4c2b-b36e-caf6450ac4d3, tutored unl-192-219 + ogn-049-298 for p1 and ogn-052/010/003-298 for p2; drove p2 units to battlefield-player-2-bf-ogn-277-298 via REST (readyCard + standardMove across two turn cycles). Relevant source: /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-cards/src/cards/unl/alpha-strike.ts (card def with split:true and amount.might object), /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/cards.ts:323-386 (spellEffectHasLegalTargets — for-each 'damaged' gate; condition ctx at ~790 omits getCardMeta), /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effect-executor.ts:167-225 (resolveAmount — might object falls through to 0) and :375-425 (damage case — no split handling). The ruling's core mechanic (355.14.e-g split distribution at resolution) is entirely unimplemented in the engine, so this is a DIVERGES rather than NOT_TESTABLE.

findings.expected: Per rule 355.14.h/.h.1: when the friendly unit's Might is reduced between finalization and resolution such that available damage < number of chosen enemy targets, the controller must drop the MINIMUM number of targets so remaining targets == current Might, and cannot drop extra targets to concentrate damage. Each remaining target receives ≥1 damage from the split pool.
findings.observed: The engine does not implement split-damage or rule 355.14.h at all. Code evidence: (1) effect-executor.ts resolveAmount() only handles amount.might === "self" — Alpha Strike's amount:{might:{controller:"friendly",type:"unit"}} falls through and returns 0, so the friendly-unit choice is never presented and the damage pool is always 0. (2) The "damage" case in executeEffect() ignores the `split: true` flag entirely and applies the full amount to EVERY target — no distribution, no ≥1-per-target constraint. (3) grep across riftbound-engine/src for 355.14 / split-damage / drop-target / cease-target returns zero hits — there is no target-drop mechanism when damage < target count, and no pendingChoice is raised for it. (4) Enemy targets are selected programmatically via quantity:"all" at resolution time, not chosen at finalization, so there is no finalized target set to drop from. Empirically, playSpell for Alpha Strike is additionally gated shut because spellEffectHasLegalTargets() treats the trailing for-each {filter:"damaged"} as a caster-chosen target requiring ≥1 already-damaged enemy unit at a battlefield — I could not get the card onto the chain even with a friendly 5-might unit and three enemy units at a battlefield.
findings.notes: Setup: goldfish game a34260b9, tutored unl-192-219 + ogn-095-298 (Stupefy) into p1 hand, spawned Mech(3M) for p1 + 3 Recruit tokens for p2 via addToken, then rotated turns to get real p2 units at a battlefield. playSpell(Alpha Strike) rejected with CONDITION_FAILED at every board state tried. Root cause traced to /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effect-executor.ts (resolveAmount lines ~183-188 falls through for might:{object}; damage handler lines ~375-425 has no split branch) and /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-cards/src/cards/unl/alpha-strike.ts (declares split:true, which nothing reads). The card file's own header comment already flags the for-each kill-tracking as a FIXME approximation. Screenshot: /tmp/ruling-013355072ffd6542.png.
